Loss-of-function mutations in PIGA disrupt the GPI anchor biosynthesis pathway, leading to a deficiency of GPI-anchored proteins. This deficiency manifests as paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and contributes to the phenotype of intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 42.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in PIGA that are exclusively associated with one disease phenotype and not the other, or demonstrating that the deficiency of GPI-anchored proteins does not directly lead to the core features of both conditions.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PIGA and GPI anchor biosynthesis in these distinct diseases could inform therapeutic strategies targeting protein anchoring or downstream consequences of its deficiency, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
